title: Unauthorised access to SLA test environment holding personal data
asked: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre asked about unauthorised access to a vendor-managed SLA test environment holding real personal data of about 70,000 people: how the data got into and stayed in a dataset meant for mock or anonymised data, when the environment was last audited against Government data-security requirements, and what contractual action may follow investigations.
response: Mr Murali Pillai said the incident involved unauthorised access to a dataset in an IBM-managed development and systems-integration testing cloud environment for STARS and ELS, separate from SLA's live systems. The dataset was created in 1998 for major system tests and updated periodically; it was meant to hold only mock and anonymised data, but SLA found it contained personal information that was not anonymised. STARS and ELS have regular audits, most recently in 2025, and contractual action will be decided after the full facts and responsibilities are established. In supplementary answers, he said SLA checked other systems and found no similar issues, and that the 2025 audit used risk-based scoping from late 2024; incomplete anonymisation was not identified, and audit reform can be considered after the investigation.
